claims: 20 m processing, output layers and ancillary/exclusion/advisory metadata; satellite ensemble and limitations. Observed Water Extent is a logical OR of flood extent and reference water; it is not wholly same-pass new detection.

claims: GloFAS/EFAS viewers, REST API, WMS, portal, STAC dissemination.

claims: STAC API URL https://stac.eodc.eu/api/v1, collection GFM, asset discovery/download workflow, Equi7Grid with 20 m pixel spacing as the working grid.

claims: Version D, DOI, 100/250 m standard Raster, PIXC aggregation, quality/uncertainty, NetCDF4 and protected-data access.

title: PO.DAAC: data use and citation policy

title: NOAA WDTD: MRMS RadarOnly QPE
claims: Radar-only QPE nominal1km, accumulation and update distinctions.

title: NOAA WDTD: MRMS MultiSensor QPE
claims: Multisensor input types, gapfill, pass distinction. Page latency descriptions are inconsistent; selected stream should be verified. NWP-filled/blended cells require explicit source-type interpretation rather than automatic independent-observation classification.

title: NOAA WDTD: MRMS gauge bias correction
claims: Gauge correction, HADS/MADIS inputs, bias-corrected product's role in v12 multisensor workflow.

title: NOAA NSSL: MRMS data access
claims: NCEP HTTP/LDM GRIB2 operational access route.

title: NOAA NSSL: MRMS program
claims: Product suite publicly available for use; software licensing is a separate matter.

title: NSF NCAR archive: NCEP/EMC 4 km Stage IV precipitation
claims: Archive-specific Stage IV support, accumulation, regional coverage changes, GRIB transition, metadata rights and DOI.

title: NOAA Water: precipitation analysis access
claims: NOAA regional analysis/mosaicking and current access context.

title: Lin and Mitchell (2005): NCEP Stage II/IV analysis and revision history
claims: Initial/revised analyses and region-dependent manual QC timing; historical methodological primary source, not complete current product specification.

title: Copernicus GFM: the new GFM archive
claims: Backprocessed archive spans 2015-01 to 2021-06; near-real-time production ramped up 2021-07. Location-dependent observation intervals are reported as 1.5–12 days. This is documentation, not an inspected current asset inventory.

title: NSIDC IMS Version 1 User Guide
claims: IMS 24 km daily analysis begins in 1997; 4 km began February 2004; 1 km began December 2014. The finest grid and earliest archive year do not describe one consistent product.

title: Wing et al. (2024), A 30 m Global Flood Inundation Model for Any Climate Scenario
claims: Protection standards are applied in post-processing in the described GFM. Some large historical events are compared with fitted local return-period composites; the authors explicitly acknowledge optimistic skill from this procedure. This documents actual practice and its limitation.

title: Smith, Patrick, Frazier and Kim (2021), Validation of Urban Flood Inundation Models Applied Using Nationally Available Data Sets: Novel Analyses of Observed High Water Information
claims: The primary study discusses the absence of consensus for handling model-dry HWM locations, identifies prior DEM-substitution and nearest-wet-cell approaches, and evaluates depth errors and hit percentages. It distinguishes on-ground from above-ground marks and shows that error metrics alone can favor underprediction.

title: Wing et al. (2021), Simulating historical flood events at the continental scale: observational validation of a large-scale hydrodynamic model
claims: Adapts a continental hazard-model framework to reproduce observed historical events and evaluates those simulations with event observations. Historical event simulations and uniform-return-period maps represent different conditions.

title: Quinn et al. (2019), The Spatial Dependence of Flood Hazard and Risk in the United States
claims: Distinguishes local uniform-return-period assumptions from spatially varying flood events and uses a stochastic dependence model, hydraulic mapping, and loss calculations. Gauge marginal distributions and aggregate loss distributions are evaluated as distinct components.

title: Watson et al. (2018), USGS Scientific Investigations Report 2018-5070
claims: The official abstract states that 2,123 HWMs were surveyed, with some averaging yielding 1,258 WSEs, and describes 19 inundation maps derived from some HWMs and gauge peaks. These are source-reported totals; no raw HWM data were acquired.

title: Iowa Environmental Mesonet: MRMS archive scope and retention
claims: Archive-provider documentation identifies NOAA cloud archival availability from October 2020, selected older fields, and a roughly 30-day hourly-ZIP cache. No selected MESH archive continuity was tested.

title: NWS WDTD: Maximum Estimated Size of Hail (MESH)
claims: Describes the 0.01-degree MESH grid, SHI input, millimetre base units versus inch display, model-temperature dependence, and storm-dependent retrieval limitations; legacy technical version note is retained.

title: NOAA-managed MRMS archive and terms in the AWS Open Data registry
claims: Identifies the public NOAA MRMS S3 archive, open-data attribution conditions and the 14 October 2020 version transition. Software licensing is distinct from data terms.

title: NCEP operational MESH GRIB2 directory
claims: Directory lists timestamped MESH GRIB2 files and a changing latest-file alias; no GRIB2 payload was acquired or decoded.

title: NOAA NCEI Storm Events Database: modern access portal
claims: Public NWS Storm Data discovery, event search and bulk-access routes; coverage endpoint changes with the archive snapshot.

title: NOAA NCEI Storm Data Bulk CSV Format
claims: Defines event IDs, time-zone fields, magnitude/type codes, and tornado dimensions. Its EF wind-range table is inconsistent with NWS EF guidance and must not be copied.

title: NOAA NCEI Storm Events bulk CSV directory
claims: Annual compressed details, locations and fatalities tables with creation-date suffixes are listed; scientific CSV payloads were not downloaded.

title: NWS Storm Report Records: collection and historical coverage
claims: Describes report sources and documented start years (tornadoes from 1950, severe thunderstorms from 1955, other events from 1996) and a 90 to 120 day publication delay.

title: NWS Eastern Region technical attachment: 2010 severe hail threshold change
claims: Documents the 5 January 2010 change in severe-hail criterion from 0.75 to 1.0 inch and discusses verification challenges.

title: NWS Enhanced Fujita scale guidance
claims: EF ratings use damage-based wind estimates; the EF scale became operational on 1 February 2007. Ratings are not direct wind measurements.

title: NWS Instruction 10-1605: Storm Data preparation and confirmation workflow (26 July 2021)
claims: Documents the NWS reporting and correction process, including SPC preliminary reports originating from local weather forecast offices and correction through Storm Data. This shared reporting workflow precludes assuming independent replication.

title: Potvin et al. (2022): Improving Estimates of U.S. Tornado Frequency by Accounting for Unreported and Underrated Tornadoes
claims: Investigates tornado underreporting and underrating associated with observer and damage-indicator availability; illustrates why raw reports are unsuitable as an unbiased census.

title: Liu, X., SPEI-GD producer R script, main branch inspected 2026-11-01.
claims: Concatenates 1982–2021 inputs, k=7 example, bare spei(vector,k), no explicit 1951–2000 fit. This does not establish downloaded product's algorithm; requires release correspondence.

title: Liu, X., Yu, S., Yang, Z., Dong, J. and Peng, J. (2024). The first global multi-timescale daily SPEI dataset from 1982 to 2021. Scientific Data 11, 223
claims: SPEI-GD uses Singer hPET; hPET seven ERA5-Land inputs; PET 0.1-degree hourly source, bilinear 0.25-degree resampling and daily integration

title: Liu, X. (2023), SPEI-GD, version v1, Zenodo.
claims: Describes a 112 GB ZIP/NetCDF distribution. The title and description give conflicting dates, and the rendered record shows no license.

title: NASA IMERG V07 Algorithm Theoretical Basis Document, 12 July 2023
claims: Documents GPCC V2022 Full Data and Monitoring inputs. A broad GPCC lineage does not establish use of the cataloged 2025 product.

title: NASA TMPA 3B42/3B43 Version 7 technical documentation
claims: Documents GPCC Full analysis Version 4 through 2010 and Monitoring Version 6 thereafter. These are historical inputs, not GPCC Monthly 2025.

title: NASA LHASA source code, master inspected 3 November 2026
claims: Default near-real-time path combines Late IMERG antecedent precipitation with Early IMERG for the most recent day; user-supplied inputs and forecast inputs are separate. The master branch can change and is not a frozen release.

title: NASA LHASA changelog, inspected 3 November 2026
claims: Release 2.1 switched default IMERG version to 07B; later unreleased entries mention 07C. Match selected code commit, stream and version before comparison.

title: Chen et al. (2023). GFED5 burned-area methodology
claims: The described GFED5 burned-area development uses Collection 6 MCD64A1 and Collection 6 MCD14ML, with period-specific treatment and higher-resolution adjustments. Do not equate this automatically to current Collection 6.1 assets.

title: Global Fire Emissions Database producer data description
claims: Producer states GFED4s used MODIS Collection 5.1 burned area, with post-2016 extensions based on active-fire conversion. Exact archived file coverage and release must still be pinned.

title: NOAA IBTrACS v04r01 release announcement, 14 June 2024
claims: NOAA release announcement documents inclusion of 2023 HURDAT2 data. Independence depends on selected storm, agency fields, revision and dates.

title: NOAA CO-OPS API URL Builder
claims: Provider tool that builds Data API requests for CO-OPS stations; links the API documentation. Example used here: The Battery (8518750), water_level, 29 to 30 Oct 2012, MLLW, GMT, metric.
